*Source: [`coded/TODO.md`](https://github.com/cpmodelai/cpat_ai/blob/main/coded/TODO.md).*

Status key: ☐ not started · ◐ in progress · ☑ done (ticked items leave at the next update; their record is [`../CAVEATS.md`](https://github.com/cpmodelai/cpat_ai/blob/main/CAVEATS.md)). **The project (user 2026-10-29): the full build of Coded CPAT**, a human-readable Python model that replicates the mitigation and distribution modules of Excel-AI number for number. Specification, design choices and the plan in words: [`cpat_documentation/project/Spec.qmd`](https://github.com/cpmodelai/cpat_ai/blob/main/coded/cpat_documentation/project/Spec.qmd) (Word copy `Spec.docx`). The phases below are the plan's checklist; section numbers refer to the spec.

## Phase 3 - Mitigation, block by block (each: equation list appendix, functions, unit tests, comparison for Egypt, register differences)

Decided 2026-10-29 (user): a block that still differs after a reasonable effort is logged (codes, years, suspected cause; `CAVEATS.md`), marked ◐, and the next block follows. Stored scenario-1 values of Excel-AI (ETS baseline CO2 `bco2`, methane activity `ch4bs`, goal-seek ETS prices `ets.ovr`) are read as data for now; once emissions are built, a check that the baseline run reproduces them. Phase 4: reference = stored values of Excel-AI Distribution 0.1.3, open items fixed as that workbook does. Phase 5 for now: 5.4 speed only (5.1-5.3 need heavy recalculations: later).

- ☑ 3.1 Header (0; macro series, matches Excel-AI) · ☑ 3.2 Policies (1; matches Excel-AI incl. the Pigouvian rows and producer subsidies) · ☑ 3.3 Prices (2; build-up and the averages over fuel use match Excel-AI) · ☑ 3.4 Power costs incl. levelised costs (3; data steps and the 722 quantity-free rows match Excel-AI) · ☑ 3.5 GDP level (16; matches Excel-AI) · ◐ 3.6 Road engineer model (5b; matches Excel-AI, scenarios 1-2; TrModel = Engineer, road fuel use of sections 3 and 5 from 5b, not yet: NotImplementedError) · ☑ 3.7 Fuel demand (5-8) and leakage, exempt use (6b; fuel | subsector table, price rows and the year step incl. biofuels and leakage match Excel-AI, scenarios 1-2) · ☑ 3.8 Power quantities and prices (3; matches Excel-AI, scenarios 1-2) · ☑ 3.9 Totals and revenues (11, 12; match Excel-AI, scenarios 1-2) · ☑ 3.10 CO2 and ETS check, other GHGs, local pollutants (13-15; match Excel-AI, scenarios 1-2) · ☑ 3.11 Module steps and GDP effects (16; GDP effects and external balance match Excel-AI, scenarios 1-2; module inputs with 3.12) · ☑ 3.12 Indicators, welfare, exports (17, 17b, 18, 19a; match Excel-AI, scenarios 1-2: every reference code of scenarios 1 and 2 is produced and matches).

## Phase 6 - Running the model

- ☑ 6.1 `run_model.py` for scenario-set files (many countries, many scenarios): `python run_model.py [set.csv] --countries --scenarios --database --out --xlsx`; writes `mitigation_<ISO>.csv` (code, variable, sector, fuel, description, unit, years) and `distribution_<ISO>.csv`; `test_run_model.py`.
- ☑ 6.2 Shiny on `cpat_model.run`: done 2026-10-29 (`cpat_shiny/server_logic/run_model.py`: the app's scenarios over Excel-AI's carbon-tax column, scenario 1 = Excel-AI's baseline; raw results, five indicators, six graphs incl. the net effect by decile, from `Results`; countries with data only; `test_shiny_app.py`; HTTP 200). Reruns compute only changed scenarios (`core/loop.py` caches each scenario run by its inputs and baseline). Left: a faster `Results.by_code` (1-2 s for three scenarios); no fuel-subsidy, ETS or feebate controls in the app.

## Excel-AI bugs (root NORMS 0 rule 6; coded NORMS 0.3)

Prototype bugs found by Coded CPAT (`../excel_ai/BUGS.md` section 2). Bugs are never replicated: Coded CPAT fixes them where the fix is obvious and lists the codes that then differ from Excel-AI in `cpat_testing/compare/known_differences.py` until Excel-AI ships the fix; otherwise it follows the prototype's fixed version. When Excel-AI ships a fix: a line here with its version, Python aligned with the prototype's fix, the known differences deleted.

**All closed (2026-10-29): Excel-AI 0.9.2 and Distribution 0.1.4 fixed M15-M17 and M19-M22; M18 withdrawn. Coded CPAT 0.9.2p0.1 is aligned with them; no known differences remain; every reference code of scenarios 1 and 2 matches.**

- ☑ M15 VAT of the year in section 18: Python and Excel-AI 0.9.2 (row `vatgen`: VAT_WEO to LastHistPriceYear, then held).
- ☑ M16 freight BEV feebate at the BEV distance: Python and Excel-AI 0.9.2.
- ☑ M17 plug-in hybrid: insurance on the BEV price, ICE maintenance (row `trimphv.pas.phv`): Python aligned with Excel-AI 0.9.2.
- ☒ M18 bus electricity: withdrawn (not a bug: all base-year bus energy electrifies with the passenger share, as legacy).
- ☑ M19 `gdpn` in bn: Python and Excel-AI 0.9.2.
- ☑ M20 gas series read by position, LNG and Europe swapped: World Bank and IEA blocks (Excel-AI 0.9.2); Python reads the IEA block by its World Bank labels (its own gas labels are swapped).
- ☑ M21 methane fee: no cap where b <= 0 or the cap overflows: Python aligned with Excel-AI 0.9.2.
- ☑ M22 Distribution percentile recycling rows: Python and Distribution 0.1.4.

## Existing open items (before the project; to be absorbed by the phases above)

Status (user 2026-10-20): the Python part was about 40% complete. Most items below are resolved by the rebuild (phases 2-4) rather than fixed in the old code; each is closed with a note when its phase is done.

- ☑ **Distribution: carbon-pricing revenue units.** (closed by phase 4.2, 2026-10-29: the new distribution module.) `derive_cp_revenue_from_scenarios` multiplies the carbon price (USD/t) by emissions (Mt), i.e. USD million, while the recycling steps treat it as local currency against household consumption in LCU; convert (exchange rate, millions) and validate against the Excel `MTOutputs` revenue. Until then recycling effects from a model run are far too small (the tests use the Excel revenue, so they are not affected).
- ☑ **Distribution: national totals.** (closed by phase 4.2, 2026-10-29: the new distribution module.) `run_distribution` passes `national_totals=None` (the survey's own population and consumption); wire population and household consumption (GDP x `distn_gdp_ratios`) once GDP exposes a real consumption series.
- ☑ **Distribution: projected electricity price.** (closed by phase 4.2, 2026-10-29: the new distribution module.) It now uses the power model's simplified price (last historical price + carbon price x emission intensity, `power.demand.rp_demand`); switch to the full electricity price build-up (legacy G1, G2) when it is ported. `EnergyPrices.ele_prices['rp']` holds historical years only.
- ☐ **Distribution in the Shiny app and the indicators** (results tables by decile).
- ☐ **Data: other oil products** fall to the 0.01 price floor in the sample data (negative retail price in 2024), so their price change is 0; check the data.
- ☐ **Data loaders**: the target format is `.pkl.bz2` (developer guide); the policies, GHGs and CH4 loaders read CSV from `DATA_PATH` until the pickles exist there.
- ☐ Port the validated mitigation logic of the Excel prototype, CPAT-AI-Mitigation-Prototype (`../excel_ai/mitigation/`; methods in `docs/methods/`), keeping the codes identical; the prototype's Python recomputations (`check_full.py`, `power_model_ref.py`, `transport_model_ref.py`, `distribution_ref.py`) are a starting point.
- ☐ **Legacy export: missing price columns and Balances.** `../data/scripts/export_to_legacy.py` leaves 48 `Prices_dom` columns blank (source/reliability flags, `taxa`, `sub.or`, production, spot prices) and cannot write the IEA flow-level `Balances` sheet; add them to the real data (or a second source) if legacy runs need them. Confirm a paste into the full legacy workbook in Excel.
- ☐ **Data workbook, CPAT format: the multi-table legacy tabs.** `../data/scripts/convert_data_workbook.py` writes 17 legacy data sheets; 21 tables are still carried in the Python layout (`py_` sheets) because their legacy tab holds several tables at fixed addresses: ECP (`existing_ct`, `existing_ets_nat`, `existing_ets_reg`, `do_ct_ets_exist`), Power (`mpp`, `lcoe_tmp`), Prices_int (`prices_int`), Elasticities (`elasticities`), Mapping (the five `distn_mapping_*`), the GHG shocks block of GHGs (`ghg_adjustments`) and tables with no legacy sheet (`co2_efs_global`, `co_benefits_ffs`, `fuel_carbon_price_inclusion`, `sectors_carbon_price_inclusion`, `global_fuel_demand`, `ic`, `int_prices_reg_assumptions`).
